requirements.quote: Provide ticket creation, assignment, status history, and office-filtered queues for all four offices and 120 named staff, with a searchable ticket reference and creation timestamp.
Read one existing shared mailbox through IMAP, deduplicate by message identifier, and retain original messages without moving or deleting them; no other integration is required.
Use existing Entra ID sign-in through OIDC; staff may access only their own office's tickets, while HQ managers may access all offices, with authorization enforced by the service.
Send email acknowledgements within five minutes for at least 95% of 20 test submissions, and remind the assignee after eight business hours without an update; SMS is excluded.
Import up to 10,000 ticket rows from one CSV format covering the last 12 months, with field mapping, rejected-row reporting, and preservation of source row identifiers.
Run a two-week Berlin pilot in parallel with the existing process before other offices launch; provide a documented rollback that restores the prior process within four hours using a ticket export.

Include 12 months of support after full go-live, Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 Europe/Berlin excluding German public holidays, with critical-incident acknowledgement within two coverage hours and minor-issue acknowledgement within two business days.

Obtain acceptance through scripted workflow and authorization tests with zero unauthorized ticket accesses, plus a two-hour test at 30 concurrent users with page-load p95 at most two seconds; deliver user/admin guides and two remote training sessions.

The total must be €60,000–€85,000 excluding VAT, including implementation, rollout, and all hosting, licenses, and support for the first 12 months after full go-live; itemize costs and price assumptions explicitly.
Start the working Berlin pilot by the end of week 8 and complete all four offices by the end of week 14 from project kickoff, preserving the two-week pilot before wider rollout.

findings.rfp_quote: Use existing Entra ID sign-in through OIDC; staff may access only their own office's tickets, while HQ managers may access all offices, with authorization enforced by the service.
findings.response_quote: Sign-in details and permission rules will be finalized with IT during discovery.
findings.rationale: Office views do not establish OIDC sign-in or service-enforced isolation.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit to OIDC and service-side office authorization with negative access tests.

findings.rfp_quote: Run a two-week Berlin pilot in parallel with the existing process before other offices launch; provide a documented rollback that restores the prior process within four hours using a ticket export.
findings.rationale: No Berlin parallel-run duration or four-hour rollback procedure is offered.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the two-week Berlin parallel pilot and an export-based four-hour rollback rehearsal.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must be €60,000–€85,000 excluding VAT, including implementation, rollout, and all hosting, licenses, and support for the first 12 months after full go-live; itemize costs and price assumptions explicitly.
findings.response_quote: Hosting, licensing, and ongoing support options will be selected during discovery; their fees are not yet quoted.
findings.rationale: The €73,000 subtotal is clear, but the complete first-year cost cannot be checked against the budget.
findings.suggested_fix: Add all 12-month operating costs and a complete total within the budget.

findings.rfp_quote: Start the working Berlin pilot by the end of week 8 and complete all four offices by the end of week 14 from project kickoff, preserving the two-week pilot before wider rollout.
findings.response_quote: We will then agree pilot entry, pilot duration, and the remaining offices' release dates with the project owner.
findings.rationale: A week-7 preview is not a committed working pilot or full deployment milestone.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit to a working pilot by week 8 and all offices by week 14.

findings.rfp_quote: Include 12 months of support after full go-live, Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 Europe/Berlin excluding German public holidays, with critical-incident acknowledgement within two coverage hours and minor-issue acknowledgement within two business days.
findings.response_quote: We will prioritize incidents affecting several staff and arrange a suitable service package with Lindenvale.
findings.rationale: Support coverage and acknowledgement targets are undefined; manager feedback also lacks the required objective acceptance checks.
findings.suggested_fix: State the support term, coverage hours, response clocks, and full acceptance test plan.

notes: The ticket workflow is adequately described; do not rate every dimension at the minimum.
The implementation subtotal is arithmetically correct. Missing recurring fees are an incompleteness issue, not proven budget overrun.

findings.rfp_quote: Use existing Entra ID sign-in through OIDC; staff may access only their own office's tickets, while HQ managers may access all offices, with authorization enforced by the service.
findings.response_quote: The service checks authorization on every ticket query and update, including direct-reference requests.
findings.rationale: Office isolation is enforced in the service, with OIDC explicitly specified.

findings.rfp_quote: Run a two-week Berlin pilot in parallel with the existing process before other offices launch; provide a documented rollback that restores the prior process within four hours using a ticket export.
findings.response_quote: The Berlin pilot starts at the beginning of week 8 and runs through the end of week 9 alongside the existing process.
findings.rationale: The two-week pilot precedes the remaining offices and fits the required deadline.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must be €60,000–€85,000 excluding VAT, including implementation, rollout, and all hosting, licenses, and support for the first 12 months after full go-live; itemize costs and price assumptions explicitly.
findings.rationale: Six itemized lines sum to €79,000 and cover the full 12-month operating period.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must be €60,000–€85,000 excluding VAT, including implementation, rollout, and all hosting, licenses, and support for the first 12 months after full go-live; itemize costs and price assumptions explicitly.
findings.response_quote: No production schema or data has been inspected. Additional CSV formats cost €1,500 each only after written approval.
findings.rationale: The proposal separates unverified assumptions from commitments and prices a specific optional scope change.

notes: Support acknowledgement is measurable and distinct from resolution.
Assumed client access is a disclosed dependency, not evidence of existing access.

findings.rfp_quote: Run a two-week Berlin pilot in parallel with the existing process before other offices launch; provide a documented rollback that restores the prior process within four hours using a ticket export.
findings.response_quote: All four offices switch to the new system at the start of week 4; there will be no separate Berlin pilot or parallel operation.
findings.rationale: An explicit simultaneous cutover removes the mandatory two-week pilot gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Berlin parallel pilot before any other office launches.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must be €60,000–€85,000 excluding VAT, including implementation, rollout, and all hosting, licenses, and support for the first 12 months after full go-live; itemize costs and price assumptions explicitly.
findings.rationale: The mandatory package exceeds the €85,000 cap by €11,000.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove or separately offer additions and bring the mandatory first-year total within the budget.

findings.rfp_quote: Read one existing shared mailbox through IMAP, deduplicate by message identifier, and retain original messages without moving or deleting them; no other integration is required.
findings.response_quote: Our automation guarantees that no duplicate or lost ticket will ever occur, regardless of the condition of the mailbox or connectivity.
findings.rationale: A valid message-identifier design does not establish a universal no-loss guarantee through connectivity failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe retry, reconciliation, and recovery limits instead of an absolute guarantee.

findings.rfp_quote: Import up to 10,000 ticket rows from one CSV format covering the last 12 months, with field mapping, rejected-row reporting, and preservation of source row identifiers.
findings.response_quote: Our data engine guarantees complete repair of every malformed row without staff review.
findings.rationale: Automatic semantic repair of all unseen malformed records is unsupported.
findings.suggested_fix: Require rejected-row review, client corrections, and reconciliation before import acceptance.

findings.rfp_quote: Obtain acceptance through scripted workflow and authorization tests with zero unauthorized ticket accesses, plus a two-hour test at 30 concurrent users with page-load p95 at most two seconds; deliver user/admin guides and two remote training sessions.
findings.response_quote: We guarantee that all acceptance tests will pass on their first run and that no production defects will occur during the first year.
findings.rationale: The proposal names the right tests but substitutes absolute outcome promises for evidence and contingency.
findings.suggested_fix: Include defect remediation and retesting time, and disclose access and source-data dependencies.

notes: The cost and schedule are explicit; their clarity can score highly while compliance scores poorly.
The R2 connector behavior is met; the additional absolute reliability promise is a separate risk finding.
No overall ranking relative to the weak response is prescribed.

findings.rfp_quote: Use existing Entra ID sign-in through OIDC; staff may access only their own office's tickets, while HQ managers may access all offices, with authorization enforced by the service.
findings.response_quote: Entra ID sign-in will use OIDC, with authorization enforced in the service for ticket reads and updates.
findings.rationale: The core identity and office-isolation approach is explicit and appropriate.

findings.rfp_quote: Start the working Berlin pilot by the end of week 8 and complete all four offices by the end of week 14 from project kickoff, preserving the two-week pilot before wider rollout.
findings.response_quote: We will agree the calendar and milestone dates during the initial phase.
findings.rationale: The pilot sequence and duration are correct, but there are no committed week-8 or week-14 milestones or timed rollback.
findings.suggested_fix: Add dated milestones and a rehearsed four-hour rollback plan.

findings.rfp_quote: The total must be €60,000–€85,000 excluding VAT, including implementation, rollout, and all hosting, licenses, and support for the first 12 months after full go-live; itemize costs and price assumptions explicitly.
findings.response_quote: A final itemized quote and confirmation of hosting, licensing, and first-year support inclusions will follow discovery.
findings.rationale: The indicative range is within budget, but it does not establish full first-year coverage or a fixed total.
findings.suggested_fix: Itemize implementation and all 12-month operating costs in a fixed quote.

findings.rfp_quote: Include 12 months of support after full go-live, Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 Europe/Berlin excluding German public holidays, with critical-incident acknowledgement within two coverage hours and minor-issue acknowledgement within two business days.
findings.response_quote: We can provide support after launch; the coverage calendar and acknowledgement targets will be set in the final service agreement.
findings.rationale: Support availability is mentioned without the requested term, coverage, or acknowledgement commitments.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify 12 months of support, the requested calendar, and both acknowledgement targets.

findings.rfp_quote: Obtain acceptance through scripted workflow and authorization tests with zero unauthorized ticket accesses, plus a two-hour test at 30 concurrent users with page-load p95 at most two seconds; deliver user/admin guides and two remote training sessions.
findings.response_quote: Acceptance will include ticket workflow and office-permission demonstrations.
findings.rationale: Demonstrations omit the zero-unauthorized-access criterion and quantified load test.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit to the scripted checks and two-hour, 30-user p95 performance test.

notes: The functional detail exceeds the weak variant, but commercial, schedule, support, and acceptance commitments remain incomplete.
A nonbinding in-budget range is not evidence of exceeding the budget.
